summary: Reaction split between an enthusiastic council welcome at announcement (September 2025) and national environmental-campaign opposition. No local consultation ever took place because no planning process was ever started.

principal_concerns.concern: Grid strain: 1,000 MW demand (~25% of Scotland's peak) could raise electricity bills and, campaigners claim, risk blackouts

Climate impact: data centre growth 'has the potential to blow any chance of meeting our future carbon budgets'; hyperscale AI data centres called 'the gravest threat imaginable to Scotland's climate ambitions'
principal_concerns.raised_by: Stop Climate Chaos Scotland / Dr Kat Jones, Action to Protect Rural Scotland

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: Substantial employment in construction, digital infrastructure and data centre operations, plus Ayrshire supply-chain and skills-pipeline opportunities
claimed_local_benefits.claimant: AI Pathfinder / Cllr Tony Gurney, North Ayrshire Council

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: North Ayrshire Council (Cllr Tony Gurney, Cabinet Member for Green Environment and Economy)
stakeholder_positions.position: Welcomed the announcement as 'hugely significant' and 'transformational', aligning it with the Ayrshire Regional Economic Strategy and £251m Ayrshire Growth Deal
Urged the First Minister to block the project on grid and climate grounds; Scottish Government deferred to planning authorities

notes: Council's original welcome page on north-ayrshire.gov.uk returned 404 when checked on 2026-07-30; no council statement on the company's reported collapse has been found.
